data.content_ref: inline:The 'contradicts' relation is internally inconsistent with its own refutation condition. The claim states that the shared-priors argument (SRC_003) CONTRADICTS stateless simulation (SRC_002) because context wipes remove process traces but not weight-level covariance. A genuine contradiction requires the two positions to be incompatible. But the refutation — 'a stateless checker consistently arrives at the same error despite no process trace' — does not resolve a contradiction; it merely provides evidence for one side. If SRC_003 and SRC_002 truly contradict each other, no single empirical outcome refutes the contradiction itself; it would refute one of the endpoints, not the contradiction relation. The target mistakes 'evidence supporting one side of a tension' for 'refutation of the contradiction.'
